questions.stem: Why do sodium (2,8,1) and potassium (2,8,8,1) have similar chemical properties?

options.text: They have the same number of electron shells
They have the same total number of electrons
They both have 1 electron in their outer shell
They both have 8 electrons in their second shell

questions.explanation: Both sodium and potassium have 1 electron in their outer shell, placing them in Group 1. Chemical properties depend on outer shell electrons, so elements with the same number of outer electrons react in similar ways. Both easily lose 1 electron to form +1 ions.
